# Game model

Board: 64x64 grid of 8px cells. Cell (r,c) center pixel = (8c+4, 8r+4).
Rows 0-9 = HUD bar (dark grey) showing a purple 3x3 icon.
Row 63 = white tick bar = resource/energy. Each ACTION6 click costs 2 ticks (64 -> 32 clicks total).
Actions: only ACTION6 (click) and ACTION7 (undo). RESET unavailable.
9 levels total.

## Core mechanic (confirmed L1)
Clicking cell (R,C) spawns a white ring of radius 8 cells centred on (R,C) that
contracts inward (a "pull field"). Any movable object whose cells lie inside the
ring is dragged and snapped so its centre lands exactly on (R,C).
- The ring appears on EVERY click, dot or not, valid or not; cost is paid anyway.
- Activation test (best fit): the nearest cell of the object must be within
  Euclidean distance 8 cells of the click cell.
- For a 3x3 object centred at (r,c), a click at (r-a, c+b) works iff
  (a-1)^2 + (b-1)^2 <= 64.  => max pure diagonal jump = 6; max (a,b) sum = 13
  e.g. (7,6) and (6,7) are legal; (7,7) and (8,5) are not.

## Level layout convention
- Purple 3x3 = the movable block.
- Blue circle with dark-grey 3x3 silhouette inside = destination; land block centre
  on the silhouette centre.
- Faint grey dots every 2 cells = suggested path; a white plus on the path marks a
  hint/first legal landing cell. Dots are only a guide, clicks work anywhere.

## Efficiency
To travel N cells diagonally, use moves of (7,6)/(6,7)/(6,6); needs ceil(2N/13) clicks.

# Game model

Board: 64x64 grid of 8px cells. Cell (r,c) center pixel = (8c+4, 8r+4).
Rows 0-9 = HUD bar. Row 63 = white tick bar = energy; each click costs 2 ticks (32 clicks/level).
Bar refills at each new level. Actions: ACTION6 (click) + ACTION7 (undo). 9 levels.

## Core mechanic: gravity click
Clicking cell (R,C) spawns a ring of radius 8 cells that contracts to (R,C).
Every movable object whose NEAREST cell lies within Euclidean distance <= 8 cells of
(R,C) is dragged and snapped onto (R,C).
- Ring/animation appears on every click; the 2-tick cost is paid even if nothing happens.
- Objects further away are untouched. Distance is measured to the object's closest cell,
  so bigger objects reach further (a 3x3 centred at (r,c) has cells at +-1).

## Placement convention
An NxN object snapped to click cell (R,C) is placed so that the click cell is its
cell index (floor(N/2), floor(N/2)) counting from the top-left:
- 2x2 -> occupies rows R-1..R, cols C-1..C   (click = bottom-right cell)
- 3x3 -> rows R-1..R+1, cols C-1..C+1        (click = centre)
- 4x4 -> rows R-2..R+1, cols C-2..C+1
Max pure-diagonal jump for a 3x3 is 6 cells; for (a,b) offsets need (a-1)^2+(b-1)^2 <= 64.

## Merging (tier chain)
cyan 1x1 -> pink 2x2 -> purple 3x3 -> yellow 4x4  (HUD top-left legend shows the chain)
Exactly TWO objects of the SAME tier pulled onto one click merge into one next-tier object.
Pulling 3 objects, or a mix of tiers, is ILLEGAL: the move animates and then fully
REVERTS (long ~21-frame animation, no net change) but still costs 2 ticks.
=> Always check which other objects lie within 8 of an intended click.

## Goal
HUD centre shows the required object(s). Blue circles are delivery targets; put the
required object on the circle's centre cell (a dark silhouette inside a circle, when
shown, marks the exact required cell). Level completes when all targets are filled.

# Game model

Board: 64x64 grid of 8px cells. Cell (r,c) centre pixel = (8c+4, 8r+4).
Rows 0-9 = HUD. Row 63 = white tick bar = energy; each click costs 2 ticks (32 clicks/level).
Actions: ACTION6 (click) and ACTION7 (undo). 9 levels.

## Core mechanic: gravity click
Clicking cell (R,C) spawns a ring of radius 8 cells that contracts to (R,C).
Every movable thing whose NEAREST cell is within Euclidean distance <= 8 of (R,C)
is dragged and snapped onto (R,C). Distance 8 works, 9 does not.
Cost is paid even if nothing moves.

## Placement convention
An NxN object snapped to click cell (R,C) is placed with the click cell at its
cell index (floor(N/2), floor(N/2)) from the top-left:
 2x2 -> rows R-1..R,  cols C-1..C
 3x3 -> rows R-1..R+1, cols C-1..C+1  (centred)
 4x4 -> rows R-2..R+1, cols C-2..C+1
 5x5 -> rows R-2..R+2, cols C-2..C+2
Entity (4 rows x 5 cols) -> rows R-1..R+2, cols C-2..C+2.

## Tier chain (HUD top-left legend)
cyan 1x1 -> pink 2x2 -> purple 3x3 -> yellow 4x4 -> orange 5x5 -> red (7x7 seen)
Exactly TWO objects of the SAME tier pulled onto one click merge into one next-tier
object. Pulling 3+ things, or a mix of tiers, is ILLEGAL: it animates then fully
REVERTS (long animation) and still costs 2 ticks.
=> Before every click, list everything whose nearest cell is within 8 of it.

## Entities (light pink #FF7BCC, 8-cell arrow, bbox 4 rows x 5 cols)
- Each turn an entity that was NOT pulled moves exactly 4 cells DIAGONALLY toward the
  nearest object.
- On contact it BITES: the object drops ONE tier and is knocked ~8 cells directly away
  from the entity. A cyan (lowest tier) is destroyed outright.
  => Biting is the only way to make small objects out of a big one (red->orange->yellow).
  => Also a hazard: never let an entity reach a finished goal object.
- Entities ARE pullable. After being pulled to a click they do NOT chase that turn;
  they continue 4 cells diagonally in the (8-way quantised) pull direction.
  Net travel per pull click ~12 cells.

## Goals
HUD centre lists the required objects; an entity icon there means an entity must be
delivered too. Blue circles are delivery slots: put the object's placement anchor on
the circle's centre cell. Level completes when every slot is filled.

# Game model — COMPLETED (9/9 levels, WIN at turn 90)

Board: 64x64 grid of 8px cells. Cell (r,c) centre pixel = (8c+4, 8r+4).
Rows 0-9 HUD; row 63 = white tick energy bar (2 ticks per click, 32 clicks/level, refills).
Only ACTION6 (click) and ACTION7 (undo) are ever available.

## Core mechanic: gravity click
Clicking cell (R,C) spawns a ring of radius 8 cells that contracts onto (R,C).
Everything whose NEAREST cell is within Euclidean distance <= 8 of (R,C) is dragged
and snapped onto (R,C). Distance 8 works, 9 does not. Cost is paid even if nothing moves.

## Placement convention
An NxN object snapped to (R,C) has the click cell at index (floor(N/2),floor(N/2)):
 2x2 rows R-1..R, cols C-1..C | 3x3 centred | 4x4 rows R-2..R+1, cols C-2..C+1
 5x5 centred | entity (4x5 bbox) rows R-2..R+1, cols C-2..C+2.
Max pure-diagonal jump for a 3x3 is 6; generally offset (a,b) needs (a-1)^2+(b-1)^2<=64.

## Tiers and merging
Objects: cyan 1x1 -> pink 2x2 -> purple 3x3 -> yellow 4x4 -> orange 5x5 -> red 7x7.
Entities: pink -> green -> dark red (second HUD legend row).
Exactly TWO things of the SAME tier pulled onto one click merge into the next tier.
Pulling 3+ things, or a mix of tiers/types, is ILLEGAL: it animates then fully REVERTS
(long animation) and still costs ticks. Always list what lies within 8 of a planned click.

## Entities
- Not pulled this turn => moves toward the NEAREST object: pink 4 cells/turn,
  dark red 8 cells/turn (speed grows with tier). Pulled => snaps to the click, no move.
- On contact it BITES: the object drops ONE tier and is knocked ~8 cells away from the
  entity. This is the only way to break a big block down (red -> orange -> yellow).
  It is also the main hazard: never let one reach a finished goal object.
- Entities are goals themselves when shown in the HUD; deliver them like objects.

## Goals
HUD centre lists required objects/entities; blue circles are the slots. The object must
lie inside the circle (exact centring is not required — full overlap suffices).
The level completes the moment all slots are simultaneously filled.
IMPORTANT: entities never rest, so a delivered entity walks out again. Deliver all
inert objects first and place the entity with the final click (or time its drift so it
is back on its circle when the last object lands).

## General tactics
- Merge pairs at the point furthest along the route to the target: a merge doubles as a move.
- Chain: choose each merge point so the product is within reach of the next merge point.
- Use an undelivered object as bait to walk entities across the board for free.
- Undo (ACTION7) exists, so a risky probe costs at most one extra action.

[After action · message]
**Game complete — WIN, 9/9 levels in 90 actions.**

How the model developed:

1. **Level 1** — Discovered the core mechanic from the animation: a click spawns a radius‑8 ring that *pulls* any object whose nearest cell is within 8 cells onto the click point. Derived the exact reach rule and solved the traversal in a provably minimal 6 moves using mixed (7,6)/(6,6) hops instead of naive 6‑cell diagonals.

2. **Levels 2–3** — Learned the tier chain (cyan→pink→purple→yellow) and the exact block‑placement convention. A failed probe taught me that pulling 3 things, or mixed tiers, is *illegal and reverts* — so every subsequent click was pre‑checked against everything within 8 cells.

3. **Levels 4–5** — Identified the entities: 4 cells/turn toward the nearest object, and they **eat** things on contact (a cyan vanished).

4. **Level 6** — The key insight: with only a red 7×7 block and no small pieces, the entity's "bite" was the *tool*, not just the hazard — it knocks an object down one tier (red→orange→yellow). Also found entities are pullable and are themselves deliverable goals.

5. **Levels 7–9** — Combined everything: bites to break blocks down, merges to build up, entity merging (pink→green→dark red), and using undelivered objects as bait to move entities for free.

The last puzzle needed one final realization: **entities never rest**, so a delivered entity walks back out. I pushed the dark‑red entity two pulls away to protect the purple, delivered the orange last, and timed its drift so it was back on its circle exactly when the final piece landed.
